declaration.parameter_mapping: The card is the standard worklist (Hopcroft–Karp-style) closure for extending a homomorphism between two deterministic automata over the alphabet {L,R}. Equivalently, it extends a morphism of finite M-sets for the free monoid M={L,R}*. Symbol by symbol: the source table T[a,i] is the source automaton's transition function delta_1(i,a). U[a,j] is the target automaton's transition function delta_2(j,a). The partial map F is the candidate homomorphism h. A demonstration seed(i,j) is the initial pair (i,j) pushed on the pending-pair stack. The FIFO_A loop pops (x,y). If h(x) is undefined, it sets h(x)=y and pushes (delta_1(x,a), delta_2(y,a)) for each letter a. If h(x)=y already, it skips. If h(x) differs from y, it reports failure. This is exactly the textbook procedure for testing whether a state pair generates a functional simulation or homomorphism. Without union-find it is the directed version of the Hopcroft–Karp 1971 DFA equivalence check, and it is congruence-closure-style propagation of the constraint h(delta_1(x,a)) = delta_2(h(x),a). The contradiction bit c is that algorithm's 'not a homomorphism' verdict. Parse_A is a fixed DFA that runs a word: r <- delta_1(r,a) letter by letter, which is ordinary automaton execution. The readout p_t is a lookup h(r), with a uniform distribution when h(r) is undefined or c is set. No component falls outside this algorithm plus a hand-coded tokenizer.

declaration.base_form: Dewey leaf insertion and ancestor prefix relation
declaration.update: A new leaf appends a sibling ordinal to the parent path. C(j)=U^j L faithfully encodes this path in the Stern-Brocot monoid. Ancestor-or-self is a path prefix, evaluated here through parent links. Three-token parsing, fresh parent roots only on accepted facts, unknown-node abstention, reflexivity and epsilon smoothing are explicit stream conventions. No reparenting, DAG ancestry or arbitrary-position insertion is asserted.

declaration.parameter_mapping:
The known form is a path-labeling scheme for ancestor queries from the XML/database literature: Dewey path labels with a prefix test, realized as Tropashko's nested-interval / continued-fraction 2x2 integer matrix encoding (Tropashko, 'Nested intervals tree encoding with continued fractions', SIGMOD Record 2005), on a Stern-Brocot/Farey interval tree.

- Card M[X] = [[a,b],[c,d]] becomes the node's matrix label. Its interval (b/d, a/c) is the nested interval.
- Card C(j) = U^j L becomes the per-child-index generator matrix. Tropashko uses a determinant -1 variant. Converting between them is a fixed change of generator basis.
- Card attach M[X] = M[Y] C(j) becomes the standard label composition: child label = parent label times child-step matrix. This is the Dewey path (j_1,...,j_D) mapped injectively into SL(2,Z>=0) by the free-monoid homomorphism j -> U^j L.
- Card readout min(adj(M[Y]) M[X]) >= 0 becomes the interval-containment test. Equivalently, it is the Dewey prefix test: Y's path is a prefix of X's path.
- Card K[Y] becomes the next-sibling counter, as in any online Dewey/ORDPATH assignment.
- The admissibility gate becomes 'insert as a leaf under an existing parent', which is the only insertion such schemes support without relabeling.
- The hash table M becomes the label store keyed by node id.

The equations coincide because unique factorization in the free monoid <U,L> makes M[X] a faithful encoding of the codeword string. 'R nonnegative' is exactly 'M[Y]'s word is a prefix of M[X]'s word', which is the Dewey prefix relation once the code is prefix-free.
